dockets.what_it_says: The Commission approved a settlement authorizing Rocky Mountain Power to enter a power purchase agreement with TerraPower subsidiary US SFR Owner, LLC for output from the 345 MW Natrium plant near Kemmerer, Wyoming. Public testimony describes flexible output from 100 to 500 MW and a projected end-2031 online date. The public price and core pricing mechanism are redacted. Publicly disclosed risk allocation says the PPA limits utility and ratepayer exposure to construction cost overruns and caps total ratepayer liability even if other expected contract elements fail. The settlement also requires PacifiCorp to model portfolios with and without the project in each IRP and IRP update, and to report plant performance and key metrics annually after the first commercial year.
dockets.microreactor_read: Not a 1-20 MW project, but the strongest current public template for a first-of-a-kind nuclear utility PPA: seller-side construction-overrun risk, a bounded ratepayer liability, recurring with-and-without-project portfolio tests, and post-operation performance reporting. The price needed to evaluate the bargain is not public.

dockets.utility: Louisiana investor-owned utilities and interested rural electric cooperatives
dockets.what_it_says: Without opposition, the Commission directed staff to review the Louisiana Advanced Nuclear Competitive Edge framework in Docket X-36987 and develop the Louisiana Advanced Nuclear Exploration program. LANE is meant to let investor-owned utilities and interested rural electric cooperatives engage qualified vendors for possible integration of SMRs, microreactors, and other advanced nuclear technologies. Staff must return a plan to the Commission. The directive states no outside contract work is anticipated. It does not approve a project, procurement, PPA, tariff, or rate recovery.
dockets.microreactor_read: Louisiana now has a regulator-directed vendor-engagement path that expressly includes microreactors and cooperatives. It is an early market-development process only; vendor qualification rules, utility obligations, customer protections, price tests, and cost allocation remain undefined.
